The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

U.S. prediction markets regulator issues demand that clashes directly with courts. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said regulated exchanges can't cut off customers state-by-state, but firms like Kalshi are under court orders to do so. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The crypto industry has found new ways to grow. Making money from them is another story. Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle are expanding into stablecoins, payments and prediction markets, but their latest earnings show how hard it is to escape crypto's boom-and-bust cycles. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Thailand moves to block Bitget as crypto exchange's local acquisition faces uncertainty. Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget’s operator, alleging it ran an unlicensed crypto exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past 65,000 estimate. The unemployment rate unexpectedly fell to 4.1%. The strong showing surely puts a December rate hike in play, but next week's inflation numbers and the fate of the stock market could prove more important. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Over $1 billion in bullish bets liquidated while ETF flows suggest no help in spot market. Your day-ahead look for Nov. 6, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin holds in narrow range, stocks bounce after strong October jobs report. Chip stocks were leading a rebound in the broader market on Friday following yesterday's washout. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $75,793 with a -0.58% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,232.83 with a -1.11% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

# Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows

Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows
John Isige

Bitcoin (BTC) is trading above $81,000 on Tuesday, aligning with a lethargic tone in the broader cryptocurrency market. The support range between $80,000-$81,000 reinforces the prevailing stability and consolidation, prompting institutional inflows. [...] Ethereum spot ETFs, on the other hand, recorded $103 million in outflows on Monday, sustaining a four-day bearish streak. Looking back, since September 29, ETH ETFs have posted only one day of inflows, totaling $25 million on October 13. [...] Institutional investors staged a comeback on Monday, with $527 million in Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), up from roughly $82 million in outflows last Friday. Broadly, cumulative inflows stand at $57.4 billion, with net assets under management at $105 billion, according to SoSoValue data. A steady inflow pattern would cushion Bitcoin against headwinds, increasing the odds of a recovery.

items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] Throughout the region, regulators are paying much closer attention to the systemic role of stablecoins — particularly their use in cross‑border payments, trade settlement, and inflation hedging — and are starting to define clearer requirements around issuance, reserve backing, redemption rights, and intermediary obligations, with FATF alignment and upcoming mutual evaluations serving as a common anchor for AML/CFT expectations and supervisory priorities.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] ## Key Points

 U.S. cryptocurrency regulation is evolving: Federal law now governs stablecoins, while broader legislation defining oversight of digital asset markets remains unresolved.
 Governments globally have adopted widely varying approaches to digital asset regulation, from permissive frameworks to outright bans.
 U.S. oversight is divided among regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, with the IRS treating cryptocurrency as property for federal tax purposes.

items.description:
